claims.text: Controlled thermomechanical treatment can tailor the temperature-dependent plastic deformation behavior of NiTi shape memory alloys.
Thermomechanical treatment tailors deformation behavior by shifting the phase balance between austenite and martensite.
As-processed NiTi is predominantly austenitic at higher temperatures.
A stepwise treatment involving controlled cooling rates, aging cycles, and cyclic annealing can fine-tune NiTi transformation temperatures.
Room temperature favors the austenitic phase under the proposed conditions.
Martensite becomes stable at temperatures below room temperature under the proposed conditions.
The evolving austenite–martensite phase boundary mediates the treatment-induced deformation response.
Temperature-induced martensitic transformation alters dislocation mobility in NiTi.
Temperature-induced martensitic transformation changes the operative plastic deformation mechanisms.
Changes in dislocation mobility and deformation mechanisms produce changes in yield strength and ductility.
Tailored thermal treatment will reproducibly shift the plastic deformation behavior of NiTi.
Treated NiTi will exhibit greater plasticity in the martensitic regime than in the austenitic state.
Treated NiTi will maintain cyclic stability while exhibiting the shifted deformation behavior.
Untreated NiTi exhibits standard shape-memory and superelastic behavior.
Untreated NiTi lacks the pronounced temperature-driven changes in plasticity predicted for treated NiTi.
The predicted effect requires a reversible phase transformation and an intact microstructure.
Excessive thermal cycling or degradation can invalidate the predicted deformation response.
